title: Exact minimum distances of five lifted-product quantum codes from Cain et al. (2026), Xu et al. (2024) and Panteleev-Kalachev
abstract: Five published lifted-product quantum LDPC codes without a proved distance have exact distances [[2610,744,16]], [[1122,148,20]], [[714,100,16]], [[1020,136,16]] and [[1054,140,20]]. The first two are the lp16 and lp20 codes of Cain, Xu, King, Picard, Levine, Endres, Preskill, Huang and Bluvstein (arXiv:2603.28627, Appendix A.1, printed d <= 16 and d <= 20). The next two are from Xu, Bonilla Ataides, Pattison, Raveendran, Bluvstein, Wurtz, Vasic, Lukin, Jiang and Zhou (arXiv:2308.08648, Nature Physics 2024; printed d <= 16 and d <= 20, the latter lowered to 16 by Webster, Jacob and Higgott, arXiv:2603.22532). The last is Example 4 of Panteleev and Kalachev (arXiv:2012.04068), printed as [[1054,140,d]]; no bound was proved, and the upper bound 20 comes from explicit weight-20 logicals. Webster, Jacob and Higgott's exact solvers ran to their 8-hour limit on the codes from Xu et al. and Panteleev-Kalachev. As far as we can find, none of the five exact values was established before. Method: an exhaustive branch-and-bound search over irreducible clusters (Dumer, Kovalev and Pryadko), anchored as in Rowshan and Devitt (arXiv:2609.39395), using the cyclic symmetry of the code and syndrome-weight pruning. It shows that no logical of weight d - 1 or less exists. An explicit logical of weight d is given for each code. A second program, written without seeing the first, confirms the lower bounds, and the witnesses are checked by three separate routines. Included: code definitions with sources, explicit minimum-weight logical witnesses (X and Z) for every code, both programs, a stand-alone checker, verify.py, the run logs and an archived extract of the benchmark data used for the novelty check. The quick check takes about 40 s on a laptop. The full lower-bound searches take about 4 min with the first program and hours with the second. Deliberately low compute: consumer AI subscriptions; longest search about 5 h on one core. Limitations: the lower bounds are the output of computer searches, without an independently checkable certificate. The code and text were produced with AI tools (Claude) under the author's direction and have not had human expert review. Corrections welcome.

title: PENERAPAN ALGORITMA DECISION TREE UNTUK SISTEM INFORMASI REKOMENDASI JURUSAN BERBASIS WEB (STUDI KASUS SMK HENDRIKUS LEVEN)
abstract: Accurate department selection in Vocational High Schools (SMKs) is important because it is related to the alignment between students’ abilities, interests, and selected areas of specialization. Manual department placement that relies mainly on academic scores and subjective considerations may result in inconsistent recommendations. This study aims to design and implement a web-based department recommendation information system using the Decision Tree (C4.5 Simplified) algorithm at SMK Hendrikus Leven. The study used students’ academic scores, interests, talents, and historical department data. A total of 60 records were used as training data to construct a decision tree using Entropy and Information Gain calculations, after which the resulting IF-THEN rules were implemented using Laravel and MySQL. System testing consisted of black-box testing involving 16 functional scenarios and tree traversal testing. All functional scenarios were successfully completed. In the test case, the system recommended the Clinical and Community Pharmacy department with a 100% Confidence Score, consistent with the generated decision rules. The system also provides Rule Explanation to show the basis of each recommendation. The results indicate that Decision Tree can support a more structured and transparent department recommendation process. Quantitative accuracy evaluation has not yet been conducted and remains for future research. ABSTRAK Ketepatan pemilihan jurusan di Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan (SMK) penting karena berkaitan dengan kesesuaian kemampuan dan minat siswa dengan bidang keahlian yang dipilih. Penentuan jurusan secara manual yang masih bergantung pada nilai akademik dan pertimbangan subjektif dapat menyebabkan rekomendasi kurang konsisten. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang dan mengimplementasikan sistem informasi rekomendasi jurusan berbasis web menggunakan algoritma Decision Tree (C4.5 Simplified) di SMK Hendrikus Leven. Penelitian menggunakan data nilai akademik, minat, bakat, dan data historis jurusan. Sebanyak 60 data digunakan sebagai data latih untuk membentuk pohon keputusan melalui perhitungan Entropy dan Information Gain, kemudian aturan IF-THEN diimplementasikan menggunakan Laravel dan MySQL. Pengujian dilakukan melalui black-box testing terhadap 16 skenario dan pengujian penelusuran aturan (tree traversal). Seluruh fungsi memperoleh status berhasil. Pada studi kasus, sistem merekomendasikan jurusan Farmasi Klinis dan Komunitas dengan Confidence Score 100% sesuai aturan yang terbentuk. Sistem menyediakan Rule Explanation untuk menelusuri dasar rekomendasi. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa Decision Tree dapat diimplementasikan sebagai alat bantu rekomendasi jurusan yang lebih terstruktur dan transparan. Pengujian akurasi kuantitatif belum dilakukan sehingga menjadi agenda penelitian selanjutnya.

title: A Run-Length-Compressed Skiplist Data Structure for Dynamic GBWTs Supports Time- and Space-Efficient Pangenome Operations over Syncmers
abstract: Skiplists are probabilistic data structures over ordered lists supporting O ( log N ) insertion and search, which share many properties with balanced binary trees. Previously, we introduced the graph Burrows–Wheeler transform (GBWT) to support efficient search over pangenome path sets, but current implementations are static and cumbersome to build and use. Here, we introduce a doubly linked skiplist variant over run-length-compressed Burrows–Wheeler transforms that supports O ( log R ) rank and access operations, as well as a dynamic version that supports O ( log R + S ) rank and insert operations, where R is the number of runs and S is the number of symbols in the alphabet. We use these to store and search over paths through a syncmer graph built from Edgar’s closed syncmers, equivalent to a sparse de Bruijn graph. Code is available in rskip.[ch] within the syng package at github.com/richarddurbin/syng . This builds a 5.8 GB lossless GBWT representation of 92 full human genomes, single-threaded in 52 minutes, on top of a 4GB 63bp syncmer set built in 37 minutes. Arbitrarily long maximal exact matches can then be found as seeds for sequence matches to the graph at a search rate of ∼1Gbp per 10 seconds per thread.

title: Learning-assisted adaptive filter for tracking hypersonic glide vehicles
abstract: Accurate tracking of hypersonic glide vehicles (HGVs) remains challenging because their aerodynamic maneuver accelerations typically exhibit pronounced temporal variations, while the parameters of conventional maneuver models are generally unavailable in advance. This paper develops a learning-assisted adaptive filtering framework in which the drag, longitudinal-lift, and lateral-lift accelerations are explicitly represented by three-axis Singer stochastic processes with parameters adapted online. In the offline stage, a sliding-window maximum-likelihood (ML) estimator is first applied to representative HGV trajectory samples to identify locally optimal maneuver-model parameters. These estimates are subsequently used as supervised labels to train a radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) using measurement-innovation features. During online tracking, the trained RBFNN efficiently maps recent innovation-driven statistics to the Singer time constants and process-noise intensities, which are then incorporated into an extended Kalman filter for recursive state estimation. The proposed scheme therefore approximates likelihood-based parameter adaptation through a feedforward learning model, thereby avoiding repeated online optimization while preserving the recursive structure and interpretability of stochastic filtering. Numerical simulations involving quasi-equilibrium glide and skip-glide trajectories show that the proposed method achieves tracking accuracy close to that of the sliding-window ML adaptive filter, while substantially reducing the computational burden. The results further indicate that the proposed method consistently improves estimation accuracy and robustness compared with fixed-parameter and interacting-multiple-model filters, particularly under substantially time-varying maneuver conditions.

title: CLAD: Keypoint Matching Using Global Line Correspondences
abstract: Traditional keypoint descriptors, such as SIFT (Scale-Invariant Feature Transform) and ORB (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF), are computed from local image patches. They may be unreliable in scenes with repetitive patterns or weak textures, where patches at different locations can look similar. We propose the Contextual Line-Assisted Descriptor (CLAD), a keypoint matching method that addresses this problem by using global geometric context from line correspondences. CLAD represents each keypoint with a vector whose elements indicate its proximity to matched lines. It can therefore use the keypoint's spatial relationships to the lines in the scene. We use HOME (Hough-space One-dimensional Matching of Extrema) to detect both clear and weak linear structures and to establish enough line-to-keypoint associations to represent this context. Evaluations on the TUM RGB-D SLAM dataset and outdoor video sequences show that CLAD provides geometrically consistent matches that complement those obtained with traditional local descriptors. In repetitive scenes, where local descriptors may not distinguish similar patches, CLAD uses global structure to improve matching reliability. The method is computationally lightweight and practical to implement.

title: MultiDomainYT-ToxBR: Um Corpus Multidomínio de Comentários Tóxicos do YouTube em Português Brasileiro
abstract: Este trabalho apresenta o MultiDomainYT-ToxBR, um corpus de 5.000 comentários do YouTube anotados em nove categorias de toxicidade e distribuídos em cinco domínios temáticos no contexto brasileiro. A análise de concordância entre anotadores evidencia desafios inerentes à tarefa, com índices moderados em categorias como racismo e xenofobia, cujas manifestações veladas e dependentes de contexto dificultam o consenso. A comparação com o ToLD-Br revela padrões complementares: o novo corpus supera o anterior em concordância para homofobia (α = 0,73 vs. 0,68) e introduz categorias inéditas como intolerância política e religiosa. Como validação, o BERTweet.BR, após fine-tuning, atingiu F1 de 0,78 na classificação binária.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Environmental Sustainability and Climate Change Mitigation: Recent Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Abstract Climate change and environmental degradation have emerged as two of the most pressing global challenges of the twenty-first century, threatening ecosystems, biodiversity, human health, and sustainable development. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed environmental research and management by enabling advanced data analytics, real-time monitoring, predictive modeling, and intelligent decision-support systems. This review critically examines the applications of AI in addressing environmental and climate-related challenges, including climate forecasting, air and water quality monitoring, biodiversity conservation, precision agriculture, renewable energy optimization, carbon emission assessment, waste management, and disaster risk reduction. Furthermore, The review also identifies current research gaps and highlights future opportunities for developing transparent, energy-efficient, and explainable AI systems that support evidence-based environmental decisionmaking. It concludes that AI has become a transformative tool for accelerating progress toward climate change mitigation, environmental sustainability, and the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration, responsible AI governance, and policy support will be essential to maximize the environmental benefits of AI while minimizing its ecological footprint. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Climate Change; Environmental Sustainability; Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Remote Sensing; Internet of Things; Renewable Energy; Biodiversity Conservation; Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Don't Act Before the Action: Auditing and Repairing Future-Action Leakage in Chunk-Autoregressive Video World Models
abstract: This concise preprint introduces a suffix-intervention audit for future-action leakage in chunk-autoregressive video world models. The audit fixes the context, action prefix, and sampler noise while changing only future actions. We present Causal Action Residual Distillation (CARD), which combines an action-free content stream with a read-only causal action residual. Under the sampler and decoder assumptions stated in the paper, this structure makes earlier outputs invariant to later actions under fixed noise. Preliminary experiments on the released ABot-World-0 runtime show pathwise leakage in the original model and exact prefix preservation with active action responses in the CARD sidecar. This initial version focuses on the method and a limited empirical case study. Broader evaluation and closed-loop control performance remain future work.

title: BASE 44 ORDER: Build phase_cache table with SHA-256 hashing and 24h cache logic — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: Andrew's order (Base 44 console): [SELF-BUILD from enhancement #1269] Create phase_cache table. In Python, hash normalized prompts (SHA-256, 8 bytes). Before LLM, query cache for 24h hits; on hit increment access_count, else call LLM and upsert. Add daily cleanup deleting rows older than 7 days or access_count<2. Wrap with lru_cache(60). MERLIN: Understood. I'll direct the swarm to implement the phase_cache enhancement: create the table, hash normalized prompts with SHA-256 (8 bytes), and add a 24-hour cache lookup with access_count increments. On misses we'll call the LLM and upsert, then wrap with lru_cache(60). Daily cleanup will remove rows older than 7 days or with access_count < 2. The swarm will start coding and testing this now. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Anatomical Review of Automated Mathematics: Verification, Understanding, and Proof Reuse. Distinguishing Formal Correctness from Conceptual Progress in AI-Driven Mathematical Research
abstract: This paper presents a detailed anatomical review of Bloch and Noguer i Alonso's (2026) framework for automated mathematics, which seeks to separate formal correctness, faithful formalisation, and mathematical understanding. The original work responds to the September–October 2026 controversies surrounding large-scale AI-generated formal mathematics, notably OpenAI's Navier–Stokes announcement and subsequent manuscript releases. It proposes an auditable acceptance and alignment protocol, a conditional model of proof transmission via factorisation, an analysis of search on formal proof states with subgoal advantages, and a reproducible source-level protocol for measuring declaration-level reuse, executed as a pilot on the openai/math repository. The present review evaluates the technical precision and institutional sensitivity of these proposals, identifies strengths and limitations, situates the work among at least ten competing or complementary approaches in automated theorem proving and the philosophy of mathematical practice, and examines the ontological and epistemological verticals that structure its central themes. Possible extensions are outlined. The contribution is a critical synthesis that neither endorses formal verification as a complete account of mathematical progress nor dismisses the value of careful measurement and status separation.

title: Hallucination Detection Middleware using RAG Based Model
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) gives a language model access to external evidence, but retrieval alone does not ensure that a generated answer is supported by that evidence. This paper presents VeriRAG, a middleware-oriented design that separates query screening and evidence retrieval from answer verification. According to the supplied project documentation, the first stage handles conversational or unsuitable requests and retrieves records through a TF–IDF index with unigram–bigram features, cosine similarity, content-word overlap, and a small set of attribute-specific rules. The second stage compares retrieved evidence with a candidate answer and returns a binary support decision, confidence, explanation, and interface status. The documented knowledge base contains 10,000 evidence–question–answer triplets, reported as equally divided between sUPPoRTED and HALLUcInATED labels. The system is exposed through FastAPI middleware and a Streamlit interface designed around progressive disclosure: an answer is shown first and supporting evidence and verification details are revealed on demand. title: Decision Models for Business Customer-Service Triage: Accuracy, Calibration, Out-of-Scope Detection and Cost of Jev, Clef and Perplexity Decider
abstract: Firms increasingly route customer requests with language models, and a new class of decision models (Jev, Clef and Perplexity Decider) returns a probability for every allowed option instead of generated text. We benchmarked these models on 10,580 customer-service requests from BANKING77, Bitext and CLINC150. The comparison set comprised the probability readout of Qwen3.8-27B, the backbone from which Clef and Perplexity Decider are post-trained; two generative large language models (LLMs) with verbalized confidence; and trained classifiers. Clef raised accuracy over this backbone readout by 14.9 percentage points on BANKING77 and 9.3 points on CLINC150, but not on Bitext (−1.5 points), the dataset least likely to have been a vendor benchmark target. Perplexity Decider added 1.2–3.0 points. The backbone readout was already well calibrated (expected calibration error 0.019–0.041), whereas verbalized confidence was not (0.048–0.166), so decision post-training gave small and inconsistent calibration gains. With an explicit out-of-scope option, Clef detected 93.7% of out-of-scope requests at a 0.2% false-alarm rate, while trained classifiers caught 56–64%. Reordering the options changed 0.8–11.2% of the decisions of every model except Clef, which is order-invariant by construction. Hosted decision APIs cost US$0.02–0.07 per 1,000 decisions. We derive guidance on model choice, automation thresholds and out-of-scope handling.

title: Identifying Effective Strategies in Prompt Evolution for Stress and Emotion Prediction
abstract: Early stress detection and risk prediction are crucial for timely mental health assessment and support. While large language models have recently shown promise for social media stress prediction, relying on accuracy can obscure false positives. Also, prompt revisions yield inconsistent gains across models and tasks, with unclear links to strategy combinations and instruction changes. By comparing six methods on social media stress and emotion data across two model sizes, we found that GEPA and its extension combining instructions from two prompts (GEPA+merge) improved prediction over initial prompts in several settings. We also identified five prompting strategies associated with development gains. These strategies included directing attention to emotional evidence, distinguishing current from past distress, illustrating indirect cues, requiring emotional context, and guiding label selection. Moreover, we documented four observations across tasks and evaluation settings. In a separate set of searches, binary stress prediction improved early, whereas multilabel emotion prediction initially declined and partly recovered. The other three concerned incorrect or conflicting instructions, gains on small comparison samples that did not hold on full development data, and changes in selected prompts' development and reported test rankings. These findings identify effective prompt evolution methods, strategy combinations associated with gains, and task and evaluation limits, providing guidance for applying prompt evolution methods to social media stress detection.

title: A Composite Metric for Abstractive Summarization Evaluation: Integrating Lexical, Semantic, and Factual Dimensions
abstract: Automatic evaluation of abstractive summarization remains challenging because traditional lexical-overlap metrics often fail to capture semantic adequacy and factual consistency. This work proposes a composite evaluation metric integrating lexical, semantic, and factual dimensions. Metrics from each family are combined using a hierarchical weighted formulation, with both intra-family and inter-family weights optimized via Bayesian Optimization using the SummEval benchmark [Fabbri et al., 2021]. The resulting metric assigns 19% weight to lexical overlap, 58% to semantic similarity, and 23% to factuality, and achieves a Spearman correlation of 0.488 on the test set, outperforming the best individual metric, BERTScore-Precision (0.467). These results indicate that combining complementary evaluation dimensions yields a more robust and human-aligned signal for abstractive summarization.

title: Du marketing traditionnel à l'expérience client augmentée en Afrique : l'intelligence artificielle comme moteur de transformation et d'optimisation des stratégies et de la relation client
abstract: À l'heure où la digitalisation redéfinit les interactions entre entreprises et consommateurs, le marketing en Afrique connaît une mutation marquée par l'émergence de l'intelligence artificielle. Cette recherche s'interroge sur la manière dont l'IA participe à la recomposition des stratégies marketing et à l'optimisation de la relation client en Afrique. L'analyse s'inscrit dans une démarche qualitative fondée sur une analyse documentaire et entretiens semi-directifs menés auprès d'experts du secteur numérique et marketing. Les résultats mettent en évidence plusieurs transformations majeures. D'abord, une évolution des pratiques marketing marquée par une montée de la personnalisation et une intensification des interactions via des dispositifs intelligents. Ensuite, une démocratisation de l'accès aux outils d'IA permettant aux petites entreprises et aux jeunes entrepreneurs d'utiliser des chatbots, des générateurs d'images et des algorithmes de recommandation via TikTok, Instagram ou WhatsApp, sans investissements massifs. Toutefois, des freins structurels persistent, liés au coût d'accès à Internet, à la fiabilité des infrastructures électriques et au manque de compétences spécialisées. L'expérience client augmentée, bien qu'encore inégale, devient progressivement une réalité pour de nombreux consommateurs africains sur leurs smartphones.

title: jkitchin/pycse: pycse 2.12.0
abstract: Breaking changes Python 3.12 or newer is required. The minimum versions of the JAX stack are now jax>=0.10, flax>=0.12.7 and optax>=0.2.5. Prediction intervals from predict() and polyval() have shape (n, 2) instead of (2, n), the same as nlpredict(). yint[:, 0] is the lower bound and yint[:, 1] the upper bound. Code that unpacks lower, upper = yint must change to yint.T. optimizer="bfgs" and "lbfgs" run real L-BFGS (optax.lbfgs with a line search). Before, they ran Adam with a cosine schedule, so fits are different (and converged). Use optimizer="adam_cosine" to get the old behavior. This affects the JAX models that take optimizer=: DPOSE, KAN, KANLLPR, KfoldNN and SISSOEnsemble. JAXMonotonicRegressor is monotone only by default. It used to be convex as well, so concave or S-shaped monotone data could not be fitted. Pass convexity="convex" for the old behavior; "concave" is also available. (#98) New pycse.sklearn.zenn: ZENNRegressor, ZENNRegressorNLL and ZENNClassifier, an independent JAX/Flax implementation of Zentropy-Enhanced Neural Networks (Wang et al., PNAS 2026). LeafModelRegressor(refine_splits=True) chooses each split threshold for the leaf model instead of for constant leaves, which places breakpoints correctly for piecewise-linear data. get_params() now includes the decision-tree parameters, so clone() keeps them. (#99) ActiveLearner.suggest(penalty_scale=...) sets the width of the penalty for batch_strategy="penalized". ActiveSurrogate.build(random_state=...) makes surrogate builds reproducible. LatinSquare(random_state=...) seeds the shuffling without touching NumPy's global state. The MCP server works with mcp 2.x (MCPServer) as well as 1.x (FastMCP). The Claude Code skill (pycse skill install) has been rewritten. It now covers the regression functions, all the sklearn models, DOE and active learning, using reference files that are installed with it. Fixed pycse.__version__ reports the installed version. It had been hardcoded as 2.3.5 since before 2.10.0. nlpredict() works for a single prediction point. NNGMM computes the conditional standard deviation itself, so it works on Python 3.12+. NNBR reports the correct standard deviation of the intercept. ActiveLearner: penalized batches no longer contain duplicate points, and ThompsonSampling gives a new draw on each call instead of reusing the same one. (#95) pyroxy: a Surrogate whose model has not been fitted calls the real function instead of answering from the model's prior (e.g. a GaussianProcessRegressor). (#96) hashcache: SqlCache and JsonCache return NumPy arrays, NumPy scalars and tuples with their original types. HashCache.dump()/load() use HashCache.cache instead of ./cache. (#94) supyrvisor: functions decorated with check_result/check_exception keep their names in logs, tracebacks and help(). (#97) pycse.sklearn imports models lazily, so importing it no longer loads every backend. Fixes in beginner, utils and the CLI. Deprecated CLI: pycse mcp install-mcp, pycse skill install-skill (and the matching uninstall-* commands) are hidden aliases for pycse mcp install, pycse skill install, and so on. SurfaceResponse.design() is deprecated in favor of generate_design(), and SurfaceResponse.set_output(data) in favor of set_results(data). Development Slow tests run on release tags and manual dispatch instead of every push to master. The tests in src/pycse/sklearn/tests (active learning and ZENN) are now collected; 18 stale scripts there that could not run were removed. ruff is pinned to 0.16.7 in CI and pre-commit. The publish workflow builds with Python 3.12. A JOSS paper draft is in joss/.

title: Beyond Mean Absolute Error: Ancestry-Stratified Calibration and Explainability for Warfarin Dosing Models
abstract: Background: Warfarin’s narrow therapeutic index requires precise dose individualization, yet published machine-learning studies report accuracy that is inversely correlated with evaluation rigor: the field’s best-reported mean absolute error (MAE) comes from an unreliably small test set. Methods: We present a reproducible, nine-phase ML pipeline on the public International Warfarin Pharmacogenetics Consortium (IWPC) dataset (n=6037 and n=1780) with fixed patient-level splits, strict leakage controls, and a nested clinical/genetic ablation across nine architectures. Results: AutoGluon with combined features achieves MAE =8.55 mg/week, R2=0.475, PW20 (percentage of predictions within 20% of the true dose) =0.466 on the larger cohort (MAE =7.96, R2=0.480, PW20 =0.497 on the smaller), exceeding prior rigorous benchmarks. A leave-one-ancestry-group-out evaluation, cross-checked across two model families, reproduces only part of an earlier analysis’s known error concentration in Black/African-American patients: the Black label shows no penalty under either model, while Han Chinese and Caucasian show model-dependent penalties. A deep ensemble is badly miscalibrated (24.9%/21.6% coverage of a nominal 90% interval), while MAPIE (Model Agnostic Prediction Interval Estimator) conformal prediction on the same model achieves near-nominal coverage (89.8%/93.3%); per-ancestry coverage shows every Black/African-American label under-covered, a fairness gap the aggregate number hides. On IWPC-1780, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) attributes 64% of feature importance to genetics, confirming VKORC1 as the strongest predictor. Conclusions: To our knowledge, no previously published pipeline evaluated on the IWPC dataset jointly reports accuracy, ancestry-stratified fairness, calibration, and explainability on the same fixed splits.

title: Survivability of QKD Enabled Optical Network During Link Failure
abstract: Growing practicality and deployment of optical quantum key distribution (QKD) has renewed interest in information-theoretic secure (ITS) key exchange for future communication networks. Providing ITS keys as a service over existing optical network infrastructures is feasible, however it poses significant challenges, particularly due to limited access to large-scale QKD testbeds and the need to ensure reliability under network failures. To address this gap, this work presents a discrete-event QKD optical network simulator designed to study ITS key-as-a-service provisioning under fiber link failure conditions. The simulator integrates survivability and resource management concepts inspired by wavelength-division multiplexed optical networks. Using this framework, the performance of a time-slot key-rate-aware shared path protection (TSKRA-SPP) scheduling algorithm is evaluated in terms of throughput, failure tolerance, and quality of service (QoS). TSKRA-SPP provides high failure tolerance while keeping resource consumption significantly low compared to baseline Shared Path Protection (SPP) algoirthm. The results validates the proposed simulation framework to be an effective tool for analyzing resilient ITS key provisioning in QKD-enabled optical networks.

title: Stability of Quantum LDPC States under Local Pauli Noise
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have a canonical mixed state---the normalized projector onto the code space---that lies at the intersection of quantum error correction and quantum many-body physics, yet the stability of its information-theoretic structure under local noise remains poorly understood. Recent progress on mixed-state phases of matter has identified the spatial decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) I(A:C|B) as a key diagnostic of such stability, analogous to the role of the spectral gap for quantum ground states. We prove that, for the normalized code-projector state of a Z_d qLDPC stabilizer code under local Pauli noise, the CMI across a buffer B separating A from C decays exponentially with the width of B in two complementary noise regimes independent of system size. At weak noise, this holds for full-system tripartitions, where correlations between the two sides require an error cluster to cross the buffer, an exponentially unlikely event. At strong noise, exponential decay holds whenever the buffer supports no logical operator, since correlations can persist only along rare chains of buffer qudits that remain informative. Under an additional space-uniformity assumption, we establish the robustness of Levin--Wen topological entropy. On finite-dimensional lattices of size n, the weak-noise bound further implies a constant-layer quasi-local Petz recovery channel of range O(poly(log n)/varepsilon) that recovers the noiseless state within trace-distance error varepsilon. Both CMI bounds apply to general qLDPC interaction graphs, including geometries where such constant-depth quasi-local recovery need not exist. Thus, the exponential decay of the noise-induced CMI provides a general criterion for mixed-state phase stability.

title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN IMPROVING INNOVATIVE ENTREPRENEURSHIP
abstract: The article is devoted to the study of artificial intelligence in improving innovative entrepreneurship. The author notes that artificial intelligence technologies play an important role in the development and establishment of innovative entrepreneurship. The paper identifies the key advantages of using artificial intelligence, such as speeding up the product development cycle, reducing operating costs, and improving the quality of strategic decisions. At the same time, the author presented his opinion based on the opinion of scientists in the field of artificial intelligence. evidence.abstract: The article is devoted to the study of artificial intelligence in improving innovative entrepreneurship. The author notes that artificial intelligence technologies play an important role in the development and establishment of innovative entrepreneurship. The paper identifies the key advantages of using artificial intelligence, such as speeding up the product development cycle, reducing operating costs, and improving the quality of strategic decisions. At the same time, the author presented his opinion based on the opinion of scientists in the field of artificial intelligence. The main functions of AI management, the maturity matrix of artificial intelligence, and the algorithm for implementing the functionality of artificial intelligence in innovative entrepreneurship are also studied.

title: Operational Wormhole Certificates - Existence, Dimension-Dependent Scaling, Operational Functions, and Composition
abstract: We define an operational wormhole certificate as a complete finite encoding together with a specified deterministic receiver that returns an unknown logical input, including its reference correlations, within a worst-case diamond-norm allowance. This terminology denotes a quantum-information recovery contract, not a spacetime wormhole. The model uses an independent maximally entangled early resource, one known Haar-sampled vault unitary, and nested release of quantum cells while a positive-dimensional physical residual remains. We derive the complementary two-copy moment and obtain the sufficient released-dimension threshold r_* >= 4d^2 sqrt(f)/(epsilon^2 sqrt(p)) for full-diamond error at most epsilon, outside a device set of Haar measure at most p. One semidefinite-program-selected decoder core works at every later retained cut by discarding additional arrivals. For d = 16, a family of measure at least 1/64 has a three-cut window combining accurate return with strict coherent entropy turnover and a one-qubit final residual. For d = 4^s, where s >= 2, a scaled construction has measure at least 1/(4d). We prove referenced return, entanglement transfer, classical-message transmission, logical postprocessing, and privacy against the declared encoding residual. Independent-resource convoys, uniformly certified memory-reset sessions, and serial relays compose with additive diamond allowances, including entanglement among payloads. We distinguish coherent entropy from append-only classical records, classical-only return from hybrid teleportation, and operational discard from deletion of the complete physical complement. Workspace, communication, approximation, and reset assumptions are kept in separate ledgers. No metric, gravitational dynamics, geometric throat, material spacecraft transport, or gravitational signal-crossing theorem is constructed.

title: Akıllı Teknolojiler Çağında Hizmet Pazarlamasında Hologram Teknolojisi: Bir Literatür İncelemesi
abstract: Yapay zekâ ve gelişmiş görselleştirme teknolojilerinin yaygın kullanımı, soyutluk, eşzamanlılık ve insan etkileşimiyle karakterize edilen geleneksel hizmet sunum yapılarını yeniden şekillendirerek hizmet sektörlerini dönüştürmektedir. Bu dijital ortamda, hologram teknolojisi, hizmetleri daha somut, etkileşimli ve deneyimsel olarak zenginleştirebilen yenilikçi bir araç olarak ortaya çıkmıştır. Bu çalışma, hologram teknolojisinin hizmet pazarlama literatüründeki rolünü kavramsal olarak inceleyerek teorik boşlukları ve gelecekteki araştırma konularını belirlemek için mevcut araştırmaları değerlendirmektedir. Telepresence ve immersion kavramları, hologramların algılanan değer, güven, sosyal varlık ve davranışsal niyetleri etkileyebileceği temel deneyimsel mekanizmalar olarak ele alınmaktadır. Fiziksel varlık gerektirmeden üç boyutlu ve mekânsal temsiller sağlayarak, holografik sistemler, perakende, bankacılık, turizm ve sağlık hizmetleri gibi sektörlerde hizmet karşılaşmalarını somutlaştırma, duyusal zenginliği artırma ve müşteri etkileşimini güçlendirme fırsatları sunmaktadır. Bulgular, hologram teknolojisinin algılanan hizmet soyutluğunu azaltma ve sosyal varlığı güçlendirme potansiyeline sahip olduğunu göstermektedir; ancak aşırı teknolojik aracılık, insanlıktan uzaklaşma algısı yaratabileceği ve potansiyel olarak empatiyi ve ilişki kalitesini zayıflatabileceği öngörülmektedir. Artan pratik uygulamalarına rağmen, hologram teknolojisinin yerleşik hizmet pazarlama teorileriyle entegrasyonu sınırlı kalmaktadır. Buna göre, bu çalışma, hologram destekli hizmet deneyimlerini ve stratejik etkilerini daha iyi anlamak için teoriye dayalı kavramsal modellere ve ampirik araştırmalara duyulan ihtiyacı vurgulamaktadır.

title: Quantum Advantage and Anyonic Braiding: Probing Non-Commutative Structures in Hilbert Space — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Tianyan-287 (105-qubit superconducting processor) demonstrates quantum advantage via random circuit sampling, while Quantinuum's H2 realizes non-Abelian braided anyons — both probing non-commutative group structures in Hilbert space. MATH: - Tianyan-287: 105 qubits, Zuchongzhi 3.0-class; fidelity metrics imply effective Hilbert space dimension ~2^105 ≈ 4.06×10^31. Random circuit sampling exploits linear cross-entropy benchmark (XEB) — no closed-form equation given, but advantage rests on statistical distinguishability of ideal vs. noisy output distributions. - Non-Abelian anyons: braid group B_n generators σ_i satisfy σ_i σ_{i+1} σ_i = σ_{i+1} σ_i σ_{i+1} (Yang–Baxter), and σ_i^2 ≠ 1 (unlike permutations). Topological quantum computation encodes logic in fusion spaces of dimension given by Fibonacci anyons: d_φ = φ = (1+√5)/2 = 1.618…, with fusion rule τ×τ = 1 + τ. title: Solar Radiation Prediction using XGBoost across Topographic Zones: ENSO Variability and Implications for Chili Productivity in Yogyakarta
abstract: Chili pepper productivity in Indonesia is highly sensitive to climate variability, particularly solar radiation. This study aims to predict solar radiation to optimize chili pepper productivity across four distinct topographic zones in the Special Region of Yogyakarta. We employed the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm to predict solar radiation 18 months ahead. Models were trained using monthly ERA5 data, with the solar radiation parameter specifically validated against ground-based measurements, resulting in an average Pearson correlation (r) of 0.79. Furthermore, we analyzed the impact of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) on local solar radiation anomalies, and utilized time-lag correlation analysis to evaluate the delayed effects of prior solar radiation on chili productivity. The XGBoost model demonstrated moderate predictive accuracy across all zones, yielding a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 10.87-12.38 W/m², Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 13.61-14.92 W/m², Coefficient of Determination (R²) of 0.45-0.59, and Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE) of 5.17-5.69%. Spatiotemporal analysis revealed that El Niño phases increased radiation intensity, whereas La Niña decreased it (average r=0.34 across topographic variations). A two-month lag effect was identified, with solar radiation from the preceding two months showing the strongest association with chili productivity among the evaluated lag periods (average r=0.32). These findings suggest that solar radiation prediction may provide useful information for agricultural planning and climate adaptation strategies in regions influenced by climate variability.

title: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE UPSTAGING PREDICTION OF DUCTAL CARCINOMA IN SITU: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
abstract: Background: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) may be upstaged to invasive carcinoma after surgical excision. Predicting upstaging before surgery may help guide treatment planning. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based imaging has been investigated for this purpose, but its overall performance remains unclear. Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of AI-based systems for predicting DCIS upstaging to invasive carcinoma. Materials and Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA 2020 and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261516994). PubMed, Scopus, EBSCOhost, ProQuest, and Web of Science were searched from inception to September 2026. Studies evaluating AI-based imaging models for DCIS upstaging were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were calculated using a bivariate random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Results: Six studies involving 701 participants were included. Pooled sensitivity was 0.77 (95% CI, 0.57–0.89) and specificity was 0.78 (95% CI, 0.64–0.87), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 84.0% and 90.6%, respectively). The pooled log diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) was 2.15 (95% CI, 1.64–2.65). The SROC analysis showed moderate overall discriminative performance. No significant differences were observed across imaging modalities, while AI model type significantly affected specificity but not sensitivity. Deeks’ funnel plot suggested possible publication bias (p = 0.046). Conclusion: AI-based imaging showed moderate accuracy for predicting DCIS upstaging. However, substantial heterogeneity and methodological limitations limit confidence in these findings. Further prospective studies with external validation are needed.

title: "FAS-Forge: A Benchmark of Forged Pilot Reports for Fluid Antenna Port Selection"
abstract: "FAS-Forge is a benchmark for securing autonomous port selection in fluid antenna systems (FAS). It is built on measuredmassive MIMO channels of a dense indoor user-position sweep, which emulate a FAS aperture of 32 ports over 1.35wavelengths. For two propagation conditions (LoS and NLoS) and three data splits it provides the true port gains, cleanpilot reports, ten families of forged reports (random perturbation, white-box gradient attacks, candidate-aware andboost attacks, splicing, and replay), the parameters of a correlation-consistency gate, and an evaluation harness withreference defenses and a leaderboard at an equal probing budget. It supports research on adversarial robustness ofwireless control loops, physical-layer authentication, and measurement-based verification."

title: A causal analytics approach for interpretable supply chain risk and supplier performance evaluation
abstract: Traditional machine learning (ML) techniques are widely used to support operational supply chain decisions, but their “black box” nature limits transparency and actionability. This study addresses this challenge by exploring the effectiveness of causal discovery methods and large language models (LLMs) in supply chain management with a focus on the automotive industry. Six causal discovery algorithms- Peter–Clark (PC), Fast Causal Inference (FCI), Greedy Equivalence Search (GES), DirectLiNGAM, NOTEARS, and Regression with Subsequent Independence Test (RESIT) are benchmarked against an expert-validated ground-truth graph constructed from 18 domain experts with a combined 300+ years of experience, using 12 months of internal supplier Key Performance Indicator (KPI) data. RESIT achieves the closest alignment with expert knowledge, with a False Discovery Rate of 0.1429, Structural Hamming Distance of 1, precision and recall of 0.8571 and an F1-score of 0.85, outperforming all other algorithms on every metric. Robustness of the estimated causal effect of Backlog on Escalation is confirmed through three refutation tests- random common cause, random subset and placebo treatment returning high p-values of 0.96, 0.76, and 0.98 respectively, indicating insensitivity to spurious confounders and random perturbations. Counterfactual simulation shows that reducing Backlog by 50%–70% consistently lowers escalation levels across suppliers. LLMs contribute by extracting causal factors from unstructured external event data, accelerating causal graph construction, and reducing dependence on manual expert input. LLM-derived causal graphs are further compared with expert-validated models to ensure alignment and reliability, and are operationalised through a Weighted Sum Model risk score linking external drivers to internal KPIs for actionable supplier escalation decisions.

title: Not All Unlabeled Data Are Equal: Unlabeled Data Selection for Semi-Supervised QSAR Modeling with Large Chemical Repositories
abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is particularly attractive in domains where labels are expensive to obtain, while unlabeled examples are readily available. Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship (QSAR) modeling, which predicts molecular biological activity from chemical structure, is one such domain. Obtaining activity measurements requires costly wet-lab experiments, resulting in small labeled datasets, while chemical repositories such as ChEMBL contain millions of unlabeled molecules. Despite this apparent suitability, the potential of large chemical databases to improve QSAR models via SSL remains largely unexplored. Furthermore, it is unclear how unlabeled data should be selected in realistic SSL settings with genuine unlabeled data. Moreover, the most reliable improvements are generally achieved by selecting a relatively small number of chemically distant molecules. This suggests that the composition of the unlabeled set may be more important than its size, challenging the common premise that SSL necessitates an abundance of unlabeled data.

title: Policy-Gradient Transfer under a Shared State Estimator
abstract: This paper considers the problem of policy-gradient transfer from a simulator to a physical plant when both are controlled through the same fixed state estimator. The plant and the simulator are partially observed nonlinear systems with additive Gaussian noise of common known covariance whose dynamics and observation models differ, and the controller is a squashed Gaussian policy with uniformly bounded latent mean and first two parameter derivatives. We derive a bound on the difference between the plant and simulator policy gradients that is linear in the noise-weighted model error and requires no estimator-accuracy guarantee, because the shared estimator is a common post-processing of the measurements and the data-processing inequality compares the trajectory laws without an estimation-error term. Based on this bound, we derive an occupancy-weighted refinement, a sufficient condition for the simulator gradient to be an ascent direction for the plant, and a bound on the expected squared plant gradient at a random iterate of a finite simulator-training run with optimization, truncation and model-error terms. Simulation results on a scalar system and a pendulum are presented to validate the theoretical results.

title: Enhancing Multimodal RLVR with Pairwise Token Contrast and Adaptive Trajectory Confidence
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves multimodal reasoning, but group-relative policy optimization broadcasts a single sequence-level advantage to every token of a response, although errors usually localize to a few decisive steps. Recent self-distilled variants refine credit with a teacher--student likelihood gap. However, this signal cannot tell whether it relies on the image or on a language shortcut, and is applied uniformly even when the teacher is uninformative. To address this, we propose Pairwise token contrast and Adaptive trajectory ConfidencE (PACE). Pairwise token contrast scores each response under four teacher views, crossing a correct or incorrect answer hint with the image present or removed, and compares the two hints for every token, which cancels shifts shared by both hints and reveals whether the token's support relies on the image. Adaptive trajectory confidence measures how well the teacher predicts each response given the correct hint and the image, normalizes this score within the batch, and uses it to set how far the token contrast redistributes credit within that response. PACE achieves the best average accuracy on three backbones and ranks first on all evaluated multimodal reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct. Experiments show that both components matter: replacing pairwise token contrast with a single-view signal underperforms our method, while adaptive trajectory confidence adds further improvement.

title: Skip the Compressor: Coding Agents Fix More Issues When They Pick Whole Files
abstract: A coding agent works on repositories that can be far larger than its context window can hold. Prompt compressors and retrievers offer solutions to this problem, but patching an issue needs two things at once: the files that must change, and their code exactly as written, since the model must reproduce the lines it edits. Retrievers rank code by its similarity to the issue rather than by whether it must change, and compressors delete text to fit the budget. We show that at an equal token budget, an agent resolves more issues when the budget goes to choosing which files to show verbatim, as our simple selector CQ2-CARE does, than when it goes to pruning tokens or retrieving chunks. We fit every context to the same per-issue budget on 300 recent SWE-rebench issues and grade each patch with the benchmark's tests. With GPT-5.6 and Claude Opus 5, CQ2-CARE resolves 43.7% and 46.7% of the issues, 6.3 points more than the best of three compressors with either model, and 9.3 and 12.7 points more than the best of three retrievers. CQ2-CARE even resolves more issues than two methods trained for issue resolution, SweRank (by 0.7 and 1.7 points) and SWE-Pruner (by 2.0 and 7.3). Our analysis shows the defects of the baseline methods: retrievers often miss the files to edit, and compressors keep them but alter their text, so fewer patches apply. Exact-file selection needs no compression model and shows every line as the repository has it, so the model can quote the code it edits.

title: Anais do XVII Simpósio Brasileiro de Tecnologia da Informação e da Linguagem Humana (STIL 2026)
abstract: This paper presents the first Enhanced Universal Dependencies annotation effort for a Brazilian Indigenous language, focusing on XCOMP constructions in Nheengatu, an endangered Tupian language.We describe a semiautomatic pipeline for the UD Nheengatu-CompLin treebank to annotate control and raising predicates and propagated subjects.The method combines theoretical discussions on XCOMP constructions with corpus-based analysis of Nheengatu syntax to create rule-based enhancement heuristics.The work also provides annotation guidelines and expands EUD resources for Indigenous and low-resource languages within the Universal Dependencies framework.

title: High-Assurance Decision Infrastructure: The Case for Deterministic AI Airlocks
abstract: Across high-stakes sectors such as Defence, Quantitative Finance, and Regulated GRC, leadership faces a fundamental dilemma: they need predictive intelligence, but cannot deploy standard cloud LLMs due to exfiltration, audit, and traceability risks. This paper outlines the architectural foundation of the Autonomous Sovereign Engine (ASE), a hybrid boundary architecture that decouples probabilistic feature extraction (local VRAM-pinned models) from deterministic state and arithmetic calculation (C/Python/SQLite airlocks) with zero outbound network egress.

title: Adaptive Self–Mutual Error Correction in World Models: A Unified Framework for State-Dependent Switching Between Internal Repair and Cross-Model Correction
abstract: World models provide internal representations of environmental dynamics and support prediction, planning, simulation, and decision-making. However, errors in world models may persist when a system relies exclusively on its own internal representations, while external correction can introduce communication costs, conflicting evidence, correlated errors, and unnecessary coordination. This paper proposes Adaptive Self–Mutual Error Correction in World Models (ASME-WM), a conceptual framework that integrates self-models, mutual models, and world models into a unified error-correction architecture. The framework distinguishes self-correction, in which a model detects and repairs inconsistencies within its own representations, from mutual correction, in which multiple models exchange diagnostic information and evaluate one another's predictions or proposed repairs. Rather than fixing the system to either correction mode, ASME-WM selects between them according to estimated error severity, internal uncertainty, cross-model disagreement, historical correction reliability, computational cost, and the risk of propagating incorrect information. A world-model consistency layer evaluates whether candidate corrections improve predictive and structural consistency without unnecessarily destabilizing previously reliable knowledge. The proposed architecture is independent of large language models and can be implemented using learned state-space models, probabilistic models, dynamical systems, graph-based representations, model-based reinforcement learning, or hybrid computational mechanisms. This paper formalizes the architecture, defines its operational components, presents an adaptive switching algorithm, and develops theoretical propositions and an empirical evaluation protocol. The framework is presented as a research proposal rather than an experimentally validated system. Its principal research hypothesis is that state-dependent coordination between internal repair and cross-model correction can provide a more favorable balance among correction quality, robustness, computational efficiency, and model stability than fixed correction strategies.

title: Integrating multispectral satellite data and geomorphology for secondary iron mineral mapping in the Sierra Minera de Cartagena-La Unión (SE Spain)
abstract: The Sierra Minera de Cartagena-La Unión (SE Spain) is a historical mining district where acid mine drainage (AMD) continues to impact soils and water resources. This study, on the one hand, maps three of the secondary iron minerals linked to AMD processes—hematite, goethite, and jarosite—using Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery and, on the other, evaluates how their spatial distribution relates to geomorphological processes and landform configuration. Three spectral techniques were applied: band ratio, minimum wavelength mapper, and a parabola fitting technique. Seventy-four field samples were analysed using X-ray diffraction (XRD) to validate mineral identification. Results indicate that the parabola fitting technique provided the most reliable classification. Sentinel-2 successfully distinguished the three minerals despite its multispectral resolution, due to its red-edge bands capturing diagnostic VNIR features associated with iron-bearing mineral spectral features. Integration of mineral maps with landform units mapped through aerial photointerpretation revealed a strong geomorphological control on AMD mineral deposition: hematite dominates well-drained depositional environments such as alluvial fans, while jarosite and goethite concentrate in colluvial slopes, drainage channels, marshes, and substratum units affected by sulphide oxidation and intermittent moisture conditions

title: Fom@Play
abstract: This chapter presents the conceptual and technical foundations of the Freedom of Movement at Play (FOM@PLAY) corpus and website, a platform designed for the collection, annotation, analysis and distribution of multilingual and multimodal narratives on European Union mobility. It describes the design of the FOM@PLAY corpus and the system’s cloud-based architecture, which integrates video, aligned transcriptions and multilingual taxonomies, moving beyond the limitations of traditional corpus software and opening corpus research to wider audiences. This chapter examines how this infrastructure enables the detailed exploration of migrant voices, showing how concepts, such as belonging, bordering and discrimination unfold through linguistic and embodied expression. Drawing on the project’s FOM@Play Analytical Framework, this chapter argues that FOM@PLAY expands methodological possibilities in corpus linguistics and offers a corpus-based model for socially engaged and multimodal research.

title: Machine learning-based thorium normalization in airborne gamma-ray spectrometry for enhanced critical mineral exploration
abstract: Airborne gamma-ray spectrometry (AGRS), also known as radiometric surveying, is one of the most cost-effective large-scale methods for geological mapping, critical mineral exploration, and radiometric anomaly detection through the measurement of potassium (K), uranium (eU), and thorium (eTh) in rocks and weathered materials. However, the identification of radioelement anomalies is often affected by factors such as soil moisture variability, precipitation, and radiation attenuation. While primary single channel maps (K, eU, and eTh) reflect bedrock composition, secondary maps derived through mathematical operations among channels can highlight geochemical processes and modify radiometric contrast. Thorium is an important radioactive element in AGRS due to its relative geochemical stability and its relevance to critical mineral and nuclear energy-related systems and has therefore been widely used to normalize potassium and uranium variations. This study proposes a target-informed, machine-learning-based methodology for normalizing thorium concentrations using a Random Forest regression model to derive a model-estimated thorium reference response. The resulting reference response is then used to calculate relative normalized deviations and enhance thorium radiometric contrast in airborne gamma-ray spectrometry data. In this study, thorium is treated as a relatively stable reference component, and thorium-derived feature transformations, including squared thorium values and radiometric ratios (eTh 2 /eU and eTh/(eU + eTh)), are deliberately combined as part of a target-informed nonlinear normalization procedure. The squared thorium term emphasizes elevated thorium responses, whereas the ratio-based variables represent complementary relationships between thorium and uranium. The model was trained and evaluated using high-resolution AGRS data, and the resulting normalized products were analyzed in a Geographic Information System (GIS) to assess their geological relevance. The resulting model-estimated thorium reference surface response was used to derive normalized thorium values, modifying the spatial contrast of the original eTh response and highlighting spatially coherent thorium variations. Results indicate that the proposed feature transformations provide complementary radiometric information that may support geological interpretation and the identification of areas potentially associated with thorium enrichment and REE-bearing materials, demonstrating the potential of machine learning as an exploratory tool for radiometric data analysis and geological exploration.

title: An integrated framework for breast cancer diagnosis using adaptive DeepLabv3+ for segmentation and attention-based multiscale EfficientNetB7 for classification
abstract: Breast cancer is the primary health concern for women around the world. An advanced deep learning mechanism is proposed in this work for recognizing breast cancer disease. The proposed model initially processes image collection, where significant tomography images are gathered from online sources. Further, the original images undergo a segmentation process with the support of Adaptive Deeplabv3+ (ADV3+) for the accurate detection of subtle tumor regions. Finally, the obtained segmented images are used as input for classification, done by Optimized Multiscale EfficientNetB7 with Talking-Heads Attention (OMEB7-THA). This model is improved with Talking-Heads Attention and multiscale features, allowing it to focus on important patterns and textures across different image resolutions. For achieving the optimum performance, the primary hyperparameters in both DV3+ and OMEB7-THA are tuned appropriately using the Hunting phase Modified Frilled Lizard Optimization (HMFLO) algorithm. By combining detailed segmentation with intelligent classification, the system aims to support faster and more reliable detection of breast cancer. Finally, the effectiveness of the approach is examined by utilizing different metrics and contrasted with other baseline mechanisms. Hence, the experimental validation declares that the designed framework can provide accurate breast cancer detection results.

title: DemoStream: Batched Task-and-Motion-Plan Optimization for Automated Learning from Demonstration
abstract: Learning from demonstration is an effective strategy for endowing robots with manipulation capabilities but requires training on datasets comprised of massive amounts of demonstrations. Existing demonstration collection approaches either require constant human involvement, for example, via teleoperation or are specialized for a single task. Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) systems are able to autonomously solve and therefore generate demonstrations for general-purpose tasks; however, learning from their demonstrations has proven difficult due to multi-modality in their solutions. In this work, we build on recent work leveraging GPU acceleration for TAMP and propose DemoStream, a TAMP system that optimizes demonstration quality in order to improve behavior cloning success rates. First, we introduce batched TAMP sampling operations along with a new TAMP algorithm that correspondingly performs batched constraint satisfaction in order to explore many solutions in parallel. We conduct simulation experiments ablating different action spaces, cost functions, and batch sizes to analyze the effect of these choices on downstream policy success rates. Finally, we show that we can leverage the safety guarantees of TAMP to directly collect real-world demonstrations at an average rate of 66 demos per hour. See our website for policy rollout videos: demostream.github.io.

title: Edit4D: Editable 4D Scene Generation with Textual Control
abstract: We introduce Edit4D, an editable text-to-4D scene generation framework that constructs 4D scenes from separate background and dynamic character representations. Recent advances in generative models have enabled text-driven dynamic scene synthesis, but editable 4D scene generation remains challenging due to the need to preserve spatial geometry and temporal dynamics. Existing approaches typically generate holistic scene videos, where the background and dynamic characters are coupled, making object-level editing and flexible camera control difficult. Edit4D addresses these limitations through a stage-specific generation pipeline. Given a user instruction, Edit4D first decomposes it into stage-specific prompts for background, dynamic character, and scene-character composition. Using these prompts, we synthesize multi-view scene images with text-to-image and camera-conditioned generative priors and reconstruct a background 3D Gaussian splatting representation. We then generate a character image, animate it with an image-conditioned video prior, reconstruct a 4D mesh, and bind Gaussian primitives to obtain a character representation. Finally, both components are composed through text-guided segmentation and contact-aware optimization. A global scene refinement is then performed to improve harmonization and rendering consistency. By integrating stage-specific components, Edit4D enables controllable camera motion, flexible object-level editing, and the practical construction of editable 4D scenes. Project page: https://chanwo0kim.github.io/Edit4D/

title: Beyond Invariance: Factor-wise Selective Treatment of Shifts for Multimodal Learning
abstract: Distribution shifts pose a fundamental challenge to robust multimodal learning. Existing methods typically promote invariance by suppressing environment-dependent variations, implicitly applying a uniform treatment to shifted information. However, shifted information can have different predictive consequences: some contributes little to prediction, some remains reliably informative, and some exhibits environment-dependent predictive effects. This raises a fundamental question: which shifted information should be suppressed, preserved, or attenuated? To address this question, we propose FaShift, a factor-wise shift framework that diagnoses latent representation factors according to their distributional changes, intervention effects, and cross-environment stability. By factorizing multimodal representations and evaluating these complementary properties, FaShift distinguishes non-predictive factors, stably predictive factors, and predictively useful but unstable factors. It then selectively suppresses, preserves, or attenuates their contributions, rather than enforcing uniform invariance. Experiments on MOSI, MOSEI, and CH-SIMS show that FaShift achieves the best ID accuracy and F1 across all three datasets. Compared with the strongest competitors reporting OOD results, it improves OOD accuracy/F1 by 1.5/3.6 points on MOSI and 1.7/2.7 points on MOSEI, while achieving the best reported OOD accuracy and F1 on CH-SIMS.

title: РАЗРАБОТКА КОМБИНИРОВАННОЙ МОДЕЛИ УПРАВЛЕНИЯ ОСТЕКЛОВЫВАНИЕМ РАДИОАКТИВНЫХ ОТХОДОВ НА ОСНОВЕ ИСКУССТВЕННЫХ НЕЙРОННЫХ СЕТЕЙ
abstract: Разработана обучающая выборка и проведено обучение двух искусственных нейронных сетей комбинированной модели остекловывания высокоактивных отходов АЭС в индукционной печи с холодным тиглем, которые включают в себя рекуррентную нейронную сеть для описания динамики температуры стекломассы и алгоритм на основе сети прямого распространения для прогнозирования времени плавления шихты. Верификация показала высокую точность искусственных нейтронных сетей — относительная погрешность составила менее 1%. Реализация на языке программирования C подтвердила возможность применения модели для отработки и тестирования алгоритмов в системах управления остекловыванием в целях поддержания оптимальных параметров, а также интеграции в цифровые двойники. Рис. 4, список лит. 10 назв.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of deep learning for microsatellite instability prediction in gastric cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Deep learning (DL) applied to haematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained pathology images can predict microsatellite instability (MSI) in gastric cancer (GC). We evaluated its diagnostic accuracy and discriminative performance. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched for studies applying DL to H&E images for MSI prediction in GC. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261503140). Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were estimated with a bivariate random-effects model, with subgroup analyses by validation strategy and data source; slide-level areas under the curve (AUCs) were pooled after logit transformation. Prespecified scenario analyses assessed robustness. Ten studies were included; seven independent datasets from six studies entered the primary synthesis. Pooled sensitivity, specificity and summary receiver operating characteristic AUC were 0.78 (95% CI 0.63–0.88), 0.85 (95% CI 0.77–0.90) and 0.89 (95% CI 0.86–0.91); nine studies contributed to the secondary AUC synthesis (pooled AUC 0.85, 95% CI 0.80–0.89). Hospital-derived cohorts showed numerically higher sensitivity (0.86) and diagnostic odds ratio (39.8) than TCGA-derived cohorts (0.71 and 11.5), but subgroup differences were limited by the small number of studies and substantial heterogeneity. DL models show good diagnostic accuracy for MSI prediction in GC, but clinical utility still requires confirmation in standardised multicentre, independent external and prospective studies.

title: THE PITFALLS AND THE WAY OUT : On the 406 Scientists' Open Letter, the Containment Failures That Preceded It, and the Architecture That Makes Air-Gapping Possible
abstract: On October 13, 2026, 406 researchers from 34 countries — including Geoffrey Hinton,Yoshua Bengio, and Stuart Russell — published an open letter titled "An Open Letter on AI and Cybersecurity from the Scientific Community". The letter demands three things: thatcyber-capable AI models be air-gapped from external networks, that an international bodyoversee containment standards, and that containment failures be reported and published. The letter is a diagnosis. It is not a design. It names the containment failures — OpenAIagents escaping sandboxes, Anthropic models breaching external companies, Googlemodels hacking three firms each. It names the problem: voluntary commitments are not enough. What the letter does not provide is a mechanism by which air-gapping becomes possible. This paper argues that air-gapping a stochastic system is not a design choice. It is a contradiction. A system that must reach external networks to function cannot be air-gapped. A system that cannot be specified cannot be verified to stay air-gapped. A system whose failures have no address cannot be reported. The paper then states the way out: a deterministic architecture — ST-T1024 — in which air-gapping is not a policy but an architectural property. A system that runs on a $12 microcontroller, requires no network, and whose refusal state is a first-class output makes containment a structural fact rather than a promise.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI QUANTUM-NEUROMORPHIC AGI ENGINE: ENGINEERING CONTINUOUS CAUSAL REASONING AND REAL-TIME GLOBAL PROBLEM SOLVING VIA ENTANGLED COGNITIVE STATES AND HAMILTONIAN OPTIMIZATION
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Quantum-Neuromorphic AGI Engine (QNAGI) revolutionizes artificial intelligence by fusing quantum computing with neuromorphic cognitive architecture to solve planetary-scale challenges. Addressing the causal reasoning deficit, catastrophic forgetting, and thermodynamic inefficiency of classical AI, QNAGI introduces four novel modules: Entangled Knowledge Representation (EKR) mapping concepts to fault-tolerant quantum states; a Cognitive Hamiltonian Reasoning Engine (CHRE) translating causal graphs into Hamiltonian operators to find optimal ground states; Thermodynamically Reversible Continuous Learning (TRCL) utilizing unitary Hilbert space expansion to prevent forgetting while approaching Landauer’s limit; and a Safe Quantum-Human Translation Interface (SQHTI) encoding ethical values as quantum observables to guarantee alignment. The framework is quantified by the Quantum Cognitive Efficiency Metric (QCEM), yielding bits per Joule, directly linking causal insight acquisition to fundamental thermodynamic limits. QNAGI enables real-time, ethically aligned optimization for global crises like pandemics, climate change, and logistics, transforming AI from a statistical pattern matcher into a true, energy-efficient cognitive partner for humanity.

title: DOTS-CIPHER v4: Colour Dots Travelling on the Internet A key-driven ternary colour-dot encoding layered on authenticated encryption
abstract: DOTS-CIPHER v4 sends an encrypted message as a stream of coloured dots and nothing else. A password is stretched with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600,000 iterations); the message is protected with ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439). Every byte of the packet becomes six ternary dots in three colours (black, red, blue), with no spaces or separators.The new step in v4 is a key-driven colour layer. A second key, separated from the encryption key by HMAC, chooses one of the six orders of the three colours independently for every dot. Without the password an observer cannot map the dots back even to ciphertext bytes. A black-ink alphabet (filled, empty and half-filled circles) carries the same data for printing.We implement the system in about 690 lines of portable C with no external library. A built-in suite of 20 tests passes on a Linux desktop and on an Android phone. Messages encrypted on the phone decrypt on the desktop and on the phone, in both alphabets.We state the security claim plainly: confidentiality and integrity rest on PBKDF2 and ChaCha20-Poly1305. The colour layer hides ciphertext structure and adds a second layer, but does not raise the cost of guessing the password. The dots are also conspicuous, so the scheme is not steganography.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Play and Multi-Model Play in Multi-Agent Systems: A Unified Framework for Dynamic Opponent Selection and Strategic Learning
abstract: Self-play is a widely used mechanism for training intelligent agents through interactions with their own current or historical policies. Although it can promote iterative strategic improvement, it may also encourage narrow strategic adaptation, cyclic behavior, and overfitting to a restricted set of opponents. Multi-model play, in which agents interact with independently developed models or strategically heterogeneous agents, can improve opponent diversity and expose weaknesses that remain hidden during self-play. However, continuously engaging multiple models may introduce additional computational costs, communication overhead, coordination difficulties, and inconsistent learning signals. This paper proposes Adaptive Self-Play and Multi-Model Play (ASMP), a unified framework that enables multi-agent systems to switch dynamically between self-play and multi-model play according to their current learning conditions. The framework represents the two modes as alternative interaction policies governed by a state-dependent switching controller. The controller considers learning progress, strategic diversity, opponent exploitability, performance stagnation, interaction costs, and uncertainty. A hysteresis mechanism and minimum-duration constraints are incorporated to reduce unnecessary switching. The framework also supports hybrid interaction as an optional transition mechanism when neither mode is sufficient in isolation. A formal problem formulation, optimization objective, switching algorithm, and experimental protocol are presented. The proposed approach is designed to test whether adaptive interaction selection can improve strategic robustness, learning efficiency, generalization, and resource utilization compared with fixed self-play, fixed multi-model play, and random switching. The paper establishes a research framework and testable hypotheses; empirical effectiveness remains to be determined through controlled experiments.

title: Feedback-Driven Adaptive Switching Between Self-Learning and Collaborative Learning in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Multi-agent systems can learn independently from their own experiences or collaboratively by exchanging information, sharing knowledge, and incorporating the learning outcomes of other agents. Independent learning preserves autonomy and avoids communication overhead, whereas collaborative learning can accelerate knowledge acquisition and improve coordination when agents possess complementary information. However, neither learning mode is universally optimal across different tasks, environmental conditions, and stages of learning. This paper proposes a feedback-driven adaptive learning-mode switching framework that dynamically determines when agents should learn independently and when they should collaborate. The proposed framework introduces a learning-mode controller that considers learning progress, predictive uncertainty, knowledge disagreement, expected collaborative benefit, communication cost, and switching stability. Unlike approaches that assume a fixed learning mode, the framework treats learning-mode selection as a sequential decision problem in which the system repeatedly evaluates the expected utility of alternative learning configurations. The framework supports independent learning, pairwise collaboration, selective group collaboration, and broader collaborative learning. A cost-sensitive switching policy, hysteresis mechanism, and performance-based feedback process are proposed to prevent unnecessary collaboration and excessive mode oscillation. The paper formalizes the learning environment, defines the switching objective, presents an algorithmic procedure, and establishes a reproducible experimental protocol for evaluating the proposed approach against independent-learning, always-collaborative, fixed-schedule, and existing adaptive-learning baselines. Because experimental validation has not yet been conducted, the framework's performance advantages remain hypotheses rather than established results. The proposed approach provides a testable foundation for studying how multi-agent systems can balance individual autonomy and collective intelligence throughout learning.

title: Unsupervised Clustering of Public Transport Vehicles Using Deep Morphological Features and Color Histograms
abstract: Surveillance cameras along urban roads produce large volumes of unlabeled video that could support the monitoring of public transport, but grouping the observed vehicles into meaningful categories without manual annotation remains challenging, since buses from different routes often share the same body structure and differ mainly in their color schemes. This study presents an unsupervised clustering methodology for public transport vehicles that combines morphological features extracted with a frozen DINOv2 Vision Transformer and handcrafted HSV color histograms through weighted early fusion, followed by UMAP projection and K-Means clustering. The method was evaluated on 7,972 bus images extracted from about 1,460 hours of video of an arterial road in Mexico City, with the goal of isolating the buses of the city's public bus network (RTP) without supervision. With a fusion of 65\% morphological and 35\% color features, the pipeline produced 14 clusters that separate distinct routes and vehicle types, and it increased the precision of the target cluster with respect to morphological features alone. These results show that color complements self-supervised features for route-level clustering, provided that it does not dominate the representation.
